cells: COMPLETING THE IA  |  Flexible stages and short, contextual questions
Encourage students to write and carry out their OWN mathematics rather than generating their IA.
Each stage begins with carried-forward planning information. Students review it, record new evidence, and move forward or switch tasks.
Keep prompt groups short and conditional; no forced fixed report structure, no blanket help, and no automated IA mark.
Use progress status 'Not started / Working on it / Complete / Needs review' only after explicit student confirmation.
EDITORIAL PURPOSE: Student authorship, mathematical decision-making and reflective explanation.
How would you like to continue?
Choose: Continue from Planning / Upload PDF or Word / Start without plan
Do not require a document for same-session handover.
Choose your saved IA Pathfinder planning PDF or Word document.
All fields from saved planning report
Is this still your current investigation aim and Maths course?
Aim/title, IA route, course, reason for interest
Student confirms values; none is locked.
Which of these ideas, deadlines and proposed methods have changed?
Prediction, data source/method, maths, first graph and milestones
Never mark planned data as already collected.
Do you still need any teacher guidance or permission before carrying out your method?
Yes / No / Not sure + optional explanation
Pending consent, no-data, outside-course and teacher questions
Do not assume approval when a PDF/Word was uploaded.
What would you like to work on today? If something is preventing progress, select 'I'm stuck' for one helpful alternative—not a long questionnaire.
Choose current stage / I'm stuck (C95) / Save and return later
First mathematical action, milestones and progress hints
All help can be dismissed; preserve stage and draft. Don't repeatedly present checklists or require students to solve an obstacle before continuing.
WRITE IN YOUR IA NOW: use your current aim and authentic interest to draft a concise opening in your own words. Do you want to use, edit or skip the planning note?
Write now / Already covered / Edit plan / Skip
plan.title and (where relevant) plan.route; current confirmed values
Use real aim/motivation. Preserve existing introduction prose; no invented result.
What is the minimum context or terminology your reader needs to understand why you chose this problem?
Avoid an extended background section; the introduction is deliberately brief and details can appear when needed in the exploration.
Would mentioning your original prediction and WHY help explain where you are starting?
Never force a prediction, especially if the student was unsure or on a no-data route; a prediction is not an established result. Student may update it later.
Are you working with actual collected/verified evidence or still PLANNING? If pending, write the introduction/prediction now and keep data-method ideas as Pathfinder notes.
Confirm Verified / Partial / Candidate / Pending / Theoretical; Write intro / Save
plan.route, plan.dataMode, plan.primaryMethod, plan.secondarySource; current status
Do not show a 'write collected data' prompt until data source/procedure truly used.

When you FIRST describe the method or source you ACTUALLY used in your IA, explain why [chosen method] best supports [aim] compared with [real alternative]. Does a confirmed limitation affect what can be concluded?
Write now beside method / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example

Actual selected data/source method, aim and beneficiary, relevant C24 input precision/source notes and a genuine alternative. If a new method replaces an earlier choice, remember the original decision.
Use selected statistics/census/modelling/secondary-data method; not a universal template or premature technique limitation.
Is your intended collection/source access permitted and ethically appropriate? What still needs to be confirmed?
Do not treat a planning report or teacher check-in as permission. Continue safe writing but avoid affected restricted collection before approvals.
Which initial diagram, brief calculation, compact summary or small theoretical case would most usefully reveal what to investigate next? A figure is not compulsory.
Choose suggested option / Other / None / Not ready; only propose 1–3 based on confirmed route, data, prediction and maths
Aim, beneficiary, prediction/WHY, current data status, planned first representation and chosen maths; suggestions conditional
Do not force a plot or lengthy table; use the Initial Exploration Guide. If no diagram helps, start an appropriate calculation or progress to later maths.
WRITE IN YOUR IA NOW—immediately BEFORE this real diagram or calculation: what does it help the reader investigate, and why is that useful for [aim]? Define any new symbols here.
Write before output / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
C25 variable definitions and actual input units, aim, audience and source

Show purposeful diagram/calculation introduction; bring forward relevant C24 units and measurement/source accuracy to help figure design without making a new limitations paragraph. Suppress if already explained.

For this ACTUAL figure, recall the previously recorded [quantity/units/source resolution] from C24. Are axes, scales, labels and displayed precision defensible, with the whole figure legible on one printed page?
Check figure / Already checked / Not applicable
C25 variable names and units; relevant C24 per-variable input resolution/source-precision policy; actual figure's labels, scale and source.
This is a figure-quality action, not text to paste into the IA.

WRITE DIRECTLY AFTER this ACTUAL first figure or calculation: what does it show about [current aim] and [intended beneficiary]? Compare with the original prediction if useful. Does any NEW accuracy issue change that meaning?
Write after output / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Actual output, confirmed observed feature, C23/C24 accuracy, original aim/prediction/WHY and beneficiary
Aim interpretation is the core question. Reuse C24 accuracy where relevant and mention only a new consequential limitation beside the result; routine algebra requires no separate paragraph.

NEXT LOGICAL MATHEMATICAL STEP: after the previous ACTUAL result, what did this section establish, which worthwhile mathematical question remains, and why would [chosen method] help answer it? Write the bridge BEFORE starting new maths.
Write bridge at previous result / Already covered / See 1–2 relevant ideas / Enough—conclude / Not sure
Confirmed actual feature, aim, course, existing maths considered and actual evidence
This is REPEATABLE C35 after first AND every later substantive result; no fixed number of mathematical sections, no mandatory Pearson's r or regression.

Just BEFORE this first substantial method, explain WHY [chosen technique] follows from [previous real finding] and how it helps [aim]. If calculations use earlier measured/source quantities, check [C24 recorded precision and units] as you begin.
Write before maths / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
The first exploration's observed feature and student-selected next step; course maths only if currently used

Before the mathematical section, explain WHY the chosen method helps the aim. If within the student's verified course, do not add a how-to/tutorial; if beyond it, C40L provides optional first-use explanation of unfamiliar maths in the student's own words.
Define every NEW term, variable and necessary assumption directly BEFORE its FIRST mathematical use. Are these already clear in your IA?
Define at first use / Already covered / Not relevant

Define all NEW symbols/units at first use. This is NOT a reason to teach a familiar syllabus method. Only an unfamiliar mathematical concept beyond the student's verified course needs a separate explanation of how it works.

IMMEDIATELY AFTER this meaningful ACTUAL calculation, explain what its result means for [current aim and beneficiary], at a defensible degree of reported accuracy informed by the relevant C24 inputs. Give a short local takeaway.
Write after result / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Real resultRef, actual technique, aim/prediction/beneficiary, relevant C24 source accuracy and any justified later revision of reported precision.

Primary reflection is what the real result means for the aim; after that, C40L can offer an OPTIONAL mathematical-learning insight when something was genuinely understood for the first time. Don't manufacture learning.

Does a limitation of the method you ACTUALLY used change what you can conclude about [aim]? If so, explain that consequence beside this result. Has your earlier data-source/accuracy limitation already covered it?
Write beside active maths / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Current methods, input uncertainty, mathematical assumptions and data-quality notes (not general practical difficulties)
Only NEW consequential technique-specific limitations after actual use. Earlier accuracy rules should be applied rather than restated; focus mathematical consequences, not equipment frustration.
What did your PREVIOUS substantive section actually establish? Which mathematical question now follows logically, if any?
Next question / Aim already answered / Show contextual help / Not sure
Most recent actual local takeaway; unresolved question; earlier confirmed C24 input/source accuracy policy relevant to the next technique, and any change in evidence or method.
A changed dataset or additional measurements may change uncertainty; revisit C24 and adapt the explanation of limitations, not just the calculations.
Which specific course-appropriate technique will clarify THAT unanswered question, and WHY is it a better next move than merely repeating calculations?
Choose and justify technique / Other / No next method / Show ideas

Use genuine next-method rationale. Check actual course match (within / partly beyond / outside / unsure) separately from whether the student independently researched it; no automatic sophistication benefit.

RIGHT AFTER this NEW substantial result, explain what it tells you about [aim]. Reapply the relevant earlier precision/uncertainty decision when reporting it; state any NEW method-specific limitation that affects its meaning, then record a short takeaway before choosing the next step.
Write now / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Current actual output/resultRef, aim and beneficiary, active technique, C24 accuracy/source record and any prior explanation reference, original prediction when helpful.
After an actual meaningful result, connect to aim and real mathematical consequences. Offer optional genuine mathematical insight, not a compulsory second paragraph after every routine algebra line.
In your CONCLUSION now, bring together your strongest actual findings into one best-supported answer to [aim]. What remains uncertain?
Write conclusion / Already covered / Show example
Original/current aim; student's genuine result ledger and prior evaluation notes
Synthesis only; do not re-describe individual graphs and workings.
In the CONCLUSION, explain what your combined answer means for [beneficiary], and a meaningful next question if one arises.
Write conclusion / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Beneficiary/purpose, anticipated impact, confirmed results and any essential restrictions already discussed
No recycled detailed limitations, manufactured practical impact or duplicated calculations.
Review your existing mathematical writing: are definitions, notation and logic clear at their ORIGINAL points of use? Edit those passages rather than adding a new explanation here.
Fix at original location / Already clear / Not relevant
Editorial review, not a paragraph for the IA.
Have you cited every data source and placed excessive raw data or repeated work appropriately?
Secondary source URLs, data subset and collection method
Use references and appendix without dumping full dataset into main IA.
Is your teacher's draft complete enough for meaningful feedback?

The teacher draft should be COMPLETE and student self-checked against A–E before the one permitted written feedback round. Encourage print-read, citations and readable equations/figures; no automatic grades.
Record actual teacher feedback as a PRIVATE action note. When revising the IA, change the mathematics/interpretation exactly WHERE the issue arose.
Record private action / Already addressed / Not relevant
Don't copy teacher feedback into an IA section or imply second written draft review.
What will you correct first, and how will you check it worked?
Review actual work after feedback, not automatic approval.

Before the full teacher draft and again before final submission, where can you point to evidence for Criteria A–E? Check actual mathematics at an appropriate course level and meaningful reflection throughout.
Guide: A presentation, B communication, C engagement, D reflection, E mathematics.
Have you read your finished IA, checked citations and mathematical accuracy, and confirmed deadlines?

Check current school instructions for title/identifier, consistent citation style, proofreading, page numbering, suggested spacing/length and deadlines. Print/PDF preview every graph. This is student review, not an automatic mark.
Would you like to save a progress document to reupload later?
Original plan plus confirmed changes and stage notes
Must be reimportable; not a teacher submission.
Who might benefit from knowing the answer, and why is this investigation worth doing?
Optional Use / Edit / Skip planning-note card
Suggest personal relevance in the student's own voice; avoid invented motivation or inflated claims about practical impact.
Now that you have results, what can you reasonably decide for yourself or recommend to your intended audience? What evidence supports that?
plan.prediction, plan.predictionWhy, plan.predictionImplication; current beneficiary/use and actual mathematical findings
Revisit the student's 'If this were true...' statement, then compare with real results. Advise only on what the evidence actually supports.
Does your conclusion return to who would benefit, and distinguish evidence-based advice from speculation?
plan.benefitType, plan.beneficiary, plan.intendedUse and own conclusions
An uncertain result can still be valuable; do not force unwarranted practical advice.
Try to keep your introduction comfortably under one page. A few short paragraphs—perhaps half a page or less—are often plenty.
Short note visible at start; no hard word counter or mandatory limit
Introduction guidance (not a stored plan field)
This is a helpful writing recommendation, not an IB-mandated length requirement. Detailed maths, graphs and results belong in the exploration.
Would you like to use, edit or skip your investigation aim from Planning?
Small suggested-content card: Use / Edit / Skip
Prefill the suggestion, NOT a completed prose paragraph; editing updates the confirmed planning aim, preserves drafted introduction text.
Would you like to refer to why you chose this topic, who might benefit and what the answer could help you or them decide?
Only show fields that exist. Encourage authentic purpose, not a made-up social impact; student can change the proposed beneficiary.
Would your initial prediction—and why you expected it—help explain how the investigation began?
Use only when meaningful and supplied. No obligation to state a prediction; it may be revised in the light of results.
Would one short sentence about your intended approach help orient the reader?
Outline the approach only; save calculations, methodology detail and conclusions for later sections.
It is fine—and often more engaging—to write in the first person. For example: 'I noticed…', 'I wanted to find out whether…', or 'I expect… because…'.
Short supportive hint; optional Expand examples
First person can sound natural, without a fabricated backstory. Offer optional contrast between a weak and a clearer real-purpose introduction at C10E; students must write their own wording.
You can return to your introduction at any point. As the data and mathematics develop, you may need to refine your aim, prediction, focus or description of what you are investigating.
Persistent Edit/Revisit Introduction action in stage navigation
Current aim, methods, maths, prediction and student's saved introduction draft
Never lock this stage as permanently complete; returning restores the previous draft, allowing revision without wiping other work.
Want to change an earlier planning detail? Edit the suggested aim, personal purpose or prediction, then come straight back to your introduction.
Edit planning field; confirm; Return to Introduction
Single canonical plan fields plus completion.introductionDraft
Preserve written draft; show a gentle prompt to check any text that may now be outdated. Never silently rewrite authored prose.
Have you told the reader what you want to explore and why it matters, without beginning a long explanation of your mathematics?
Optional quick self-check, not a gate
The introduction can remain a provisional draft. Do not insist on filling every suggested element before proceeding.
FIRST-PERSON INTRODUCTION EXAMPLES  |  On-demand writing support, not text for students to copy
Show these only when the student opens 'See examples'. The site should encourage authentic writing in the student's own voice; using 'I' in every sentence is not required.
This exploration investigates sleep and concentration.
I noticed that I find it harder to concentrate after a short night's sleep, so I want to explore whether the two are related.
Links a real observation to the investigation
Illustrative, not based on a student's results
The optimum dimensions of a box will be determined.
I want to find which dimensions would use the least material for a box with a fixed volume.
Avoid implying a result has already been established
It is hypothesised that a linear relationship exists.
I expect the two quantities might be related in an approximately straight-line pattern because …
Makes the student's reasoning visible without pretending to know the result
Ellipsis means student thinking, not auto-generated content
The results of the project will benefit students.
I hope the findings will help me decide how to organise my practice sessions.
Shows a specific realistic purpose or choice
Do not manufacture claims of usefulness
This project will examine a mathematical pattern.
I became curious about this pattern and want to understand why it keeps appearing.
Shows personal interest without requiring external data
Do not require a data prediction or invention
The investigation will prove the predicted model.
As I worked through my early results, I realised I needed to narrow my original question.
Illustrates that an introduction can be revisited after genuine findings
Only as an example of revision
Update own original introduction when needed
Never invent a change that didn't happen
DATA COLLECTION SUPPORT  |  Route-specific detail in the Data Collection Guide tab
Population → census or sampling → bias, nonresponse and representativeness
Only show applicable prompts; e.g., survey sampling or secondary-data provenance.
Plan fields: data sources and aims; completion fields: actual choice.
Don't force all students through a survey protocol.
Measured or estimated inputs → choice of method → assumptions, domain and model checks
Show measurement and validation only where empirical data/parameters exist.
Initial maths, source of parameters and actual model conditions.
No fake sampled data for theoretical models.
Mathematical assumptions, specialist definitions and simple test cases
No default sampling/census or instrument-precision questions.
Teacher questions, mathematical focus and assumptions.
Keep safe teacher-review pathway and reuploadable progress.
Compare realistic methods, justify choice, explain acceptable limits, accuracy, symbols and terms

Stage-gate the optional library: C20-C26 → source/sampling/measurement; C40-C50 → technique/model currently being used; C60 → revisit already confirmed constraints only. Show up to 3 relevant questions if requested, never a cross-stage mixture.
Saved progress fields include choices, precision and defined terms.
Carry accuracy through to all reported calculations and graphs.
INITIAL REPRESENTATION / CALCULATION  |  Dedicated 19-choice guide and checklist
Optional context-specific first figure, short calculation, small example or None
Match to confirmed aim, route, prediction, actual data, maths and first representation
Explain WHY; never force a graph
State the purpose; define quantities, specialist terms and units BEFORE display
Use C25 definitions, C24 accuracy notes
Avoid how-to explanations at or below course level
One concise introduction can be enough
Check all applicable visual criteria; short calculation alternative
Graph single printed page, good scale and no long table in appendix
Only diagram checks if diagram exists
No redundant repeats except aligned side-by-side
Describe actual result → accuracy only if new → aim and original prediction → investigate unexpected result → choose next mathematics and WHY
Interpretation & Next Steps I01–I26; prompts VI06–VI14
Match examples to actual observation + course; original prediction/WHY and beneficiary shown as context
C34, C34A (conditional), C34B, C34U (conditional), C35, C35H (optional)
Core reflection brief; extra checks/help only when relevant; may Save unresolved finding
No prewritten interpretation, no unstarted PMCC limitations, no quietly ignoring contradiction
Detailed checklist and conditional choices: the corresponding Pathfinder guidance section A figure earns its place by moving the exploration forward, not by being impressive or complicated.
AFTER ANY DIAGRAM OR CALCULATION  |  Observe → accuracy (when new) → aim/prediction → surprise → next maths
Immediately AFTER this ACTUAL result, describe the important observation AND why it matters for [current aim]; refer to real values, not just the procedure or graph appearance.
Write after result / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Actual student's figure/result and confirmed evidence, not predicted pattern
Only meaningful actual observation; suppress for repeated/intermediate calculations.

Earlier you established [quantity, units, source/measurement precision and any justified uncertainty] at C24. Does that rule affect the accuracy you can responsibly report for THIS result? Apply it; only write a NEW consequential effect beside the result.
Write only new effect / Already covered / Not relevant
C24 per-input resolution/source accuracy and rationale; current operation, units, derived value and earlier explanation location (if already covered).

Use sensible working precision; final derived accuracy depends on the calculation and evidence, not automatically the original number of decimal places. No fabricated uncertainty or repeated limitations paragraph.
IMMEDIATELY after this real figure/calculation, explain specifically what its value or pattern means for [current aim/beneficiary] and what question it has answered (or left unresolved).
Write at result / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Current aim and beneficiary, actual interpreted resultRef and prior output-specific accuracy/status—not a generic criterion checklist.

Aim-link comes FIRST and remains essential. After actual substantial maths, offer optional 'what did you learn mathematically?' only for an authentic change in understanding, in context beside the result.
Beside the actual result, say whether it supports, challenges or leaves [original prediction and WHY] unresolved.
Write with this result / Already covered / No original prediction
Original prediction/WHY, conditional implication, observed result
Preserve original dated prediction; one plot need not establish proof.
DIRECTLY AFTER this unexpected result, write what differs and why a particular alternative explanation or test would be worth exploring.
Write now / Already covered / Not relevant / Show example
Confirmed observation, original prediction, relevant source/assumptions
Considered ≠ tested; no fabricated reason or suppression of contrary data.

Between the previous LOCAL conclusion and the NEXT calculation, write why [chosen next technique] logically follows from [actual finding] and which new mathematical question it will answer. Use your own words.
Write bridge / Already covered / Not yet / Show example
Current observed pattern, course, aim, data and maths considered

This transition must follow the prior aim-linked conclusion and respect any established accuracy/scope boundary. Only justify the next method when it answers a real open question; do not re-list earlier limitations.
Would you like up to TWO possible logical next investigations based on the latest ACTUAL result, such as a real PMCC, fitted model, optimum or theoretical finding?
Optional Show ideas, then Choose / Other / None
Confirmed observed feature, current course, aim and data; planned maths as context only
If PMCC ACTUALLY calculated, use C35P; before computing r, only use observed scatter pattern C35B. Do not fish for a desirable correlation.
Could a justified alternative view, comparison, calculation or counterexample illuminate this unexpected result?
Optional alternative/check with reason and tested/not tested status
Actual observation, constraints, sources and current mathematics
Avoid repeated decorative plots, p-hacking or hunting only for a preferred answer.
Is your originally intended method still appropriate now that you've seen this result?
Keep / Revise / Not sure and short reason
Initial maths selections and the actual finding
Changing mathematical direction can be good reflection; don't lose the original prediction.
Offer on-demand examples from Interpretation & Next Steps only when grounded in the student's confirmed ACTUAL observations, not Planning predictions or course selections alone.
CONCLUSION  |  Reflect throughout; synthesize, communicate significance and look ahead (not a recap)
Which two or three actual findings together support the most useful overall answer?
Short combined insight, with existing result references rather than new workings
completion.reflections[].resultRef, observation, aim, actual mathematical results
SYNTHESISE, don't list every graph/table or repeat calculated steps. Results may be partly inconclusive.
Does your original expectation affect your final interpretation? If so, how?
Optional brief high-level thought; Skip supported
Original predicted outcome and reasons; earlier C34B/C34U evaluation
Never paste a duplicate evaluation of unexpected results or replace the original prediction.
What does the combined result mean for you or whoever might benefit?
Aim, beneficiary, meaning originally expected, actual findings
Don't invent an effect, prove causation by association or manufacture advice for a theoretical project.
Is there one qualification the person using your conclusion must understand?
Short scope/uncertainty note or 'Already explained adequately'
Previously confirmed data/math limitations, relevant model domain and precision
Refer to existing discussion. Do not re-list all limitations or suddenly evaluate every method in the conclusion.
What worthwhile mathematical investigation might follow naturally from what you actually found?
One or two possible next questions, or None / Not sure
Actual unresolved question, result, active methods and relevant beneficiary
Suggestions optional and matched to REAL outcomes; no generic 'more data' unless specific mathematical benefit.
What new mathematics, data or comparison would your proposed next step use—and what might that add to the original aim?
Short reason; label idea as FUTURE, not completed
Existing methods, confirmed questions and prior checks
Do not complete a new calculation in the conclusion or present work already performed as a future step.
Would anything important be lost if you deleted repeated graph descriptions, calculations, methodological details or a list of earlier limitations?
Optional editing checklist, not a writing section
Conclusion draft and references to earlier work
If no, remove repetition; one short reference to earlier evidence is enough.
Have you already reflected on important method choices, accuracy, surprises and changed direction where they actually occurred?
Self-check; one-click return to the relevant original section if needed
C20/26, C34/35, C40/C50 notes and result-ledger entries
Do NOT manufacture a large final evaluation paragraph to replace missing reflection earlier.
Does this read like a clear mathematical conclusion that draws things together and looks forward, rather than a list of everything you did?
Editable draft; no mandatory number of paragraphs
Student's own synthesis/implications/future direction and confirmed record
No generated formulaic conclusion, rigid headings, prescribed page count or prewritten advice.
Context-based possible extensions and anti-repetition checklist: the corresponding Pathfinder guidance section . Core conclusion should remain concise; offer extra help only when requested.
OPTIONAL INTRODUCTION COMPARISONS  |  Students spot what makes examples effective; never copy the sample prose
I have been fascinated by shoe sizes since childhood.
I noticed that shoe sizes vary greatly even among people of similar height, and I want to explore whether height can help predict shoe size.
Real observation creates an honest starting point, without invented lifelong passion.
Ask student what is improved, then return to their own topic.
This project is about statistics and graphs.
I want to see whether [quantity] could help [person/group] make a specific decision.
Shows an investigative aim and who could benefit, not just which techniques will be used.
[quantity] and [person/group] are placeholders, not automatically generated student prose.
First I will compute the mean, then standard deviation, then PMCC, and finally regression.
I will use measurements to investigate whether a relationship exists and whether the findings could support a useful prediction.
Helps a concise introduction unfold like a story instead of a list of syllabus techniques.
Mathematical choices can and should change after actual observations.
I will prove that taller people always have larger shoe sizes.
I expect a positive association because of my experience, but I will examine the data to find out whether it is supported.
Separates initial expectation from established evidence and gives a reason.
A first-person prediction is optional; do not force personal stories or guaranteed outcomes.
On-demand contrasts help students distinguish weak and effective introductions. Keep the main C10 journey short: purpose, aim, prediction if useful, concise draft.
SOURCE-ALIGNED MATHS, SCATTER, DRAFT & FINAL PROMPTS  |  Only stage-relevant questions appear
What mathematical question will this calculation answer and WHY is it appropriate now?
One short method reason; not a textbook explanation.
Actual result, aim and currently ACTIVE technique.
No pressure to add techniques merely for difficulty.
When technology ACTUALLY calculates something, explain WHAT it calculated and WHY beside that output—not the menu buttons.
Write beside output / Already covered / Not relevant
No technology writing prompt when not used.
Immediately AFTER the actual technology-generated result, interpret it in context with suitable units and accuracy.
Write beside output / Already covered / Not relevant
Real coefficient/result/model; data and precision record.
No invented coefficients or pasted screenshot without understanding.
Which assumption or range affects whether this tool's output can be trusted HERE?
No PMCC limitations before PMCC exists; avoid generic critique.

Does [actual chosen technique] belong to my verified maths syllabus, partly extend it, fall beyond it, or am I unsure? If beyond/uncertain, can I demonstrate understanding and seek teacher suitability guidance?
Within / Partly beyond / Beyond / Unsure / Check course with teacher
Course-level classification is a private pathway decision, not automatic IA prose. Independently researched mathematics may still be on the course. Don't claim official coverage without verification.
Can you explain why each substantial technique contributes to the aim and what the answer tells you?

In-course: apply correct maths without teaching the method; beyond-course: short first-use explanation of key mathematical principle in OWN words, with cited source and clear worked application. Always justify choice and interpret output.
Have you written clear mathematical notation using an equation editor or other proper maths formatting?
Don't require a lesson about arithmetic/plotting in the IA.
For an ACTUAL rounded or estimated result, is '=' or '≈' appropriate? Does the reported accuracy respect the relevant C24 measurement/source precision and the calculation used?
Correct exact/rounded sign and sensible precision.
Actual computed result and operation, stored C24 per-quantity units, resolution/source precision and any revised output-reporting policy.
Keep working precision; don't claim made-up measurement error.
Looking at your actual paired numerical scatter, is it clearly straight, approximately linear, curved, or showing no clear relationship?
Student-verified paired numeric plot; prior prediction just context.
No inference from predicted result and no forced PMCC.
Before PMCC: what is the observed shape of this ACTUAL paired numerical scatter? The next-step choice may be different AFTER r is genuinely calculated.
Own next action or None; optional 1–2 matching hints.
Observed scatter (C35B) is separate from interpreted real Pearson coefficient (C35P); don't show r/its limitations for only a planned PMCC.
What worthwhile mathematical question follows from the last actual section's mini-conclusion, or does the current investigation already have enough relevant mathematics?
Actual writing and school's draft milestone.
Actual PMCC triggers C35P on request; students choose and justify another method or stop, with course suitability and data evidence.
Can you point to evidence of A Presentation, B Communication, C Engagement, D Reflection, E Mathematics?
Written IA; school guide criteria and maximums.
Do not generate numerical grade predictions.
Have you printed or previewed the draft and found any unclear or split diagrams/equations?
Optional peer and non-mathematician reading notes.
Correct actual layout, not a hypothetical preview.
Are you preparing for the school's one permitted round of written teacher feedback?
Do not invite second written draft feedback or claim school submission.
Are data, graphics and ideas cited consistently, and does the IA read like your own work?
2025 guide suggests MLA in Google Docs; follow current school/teacher style.
After feedback and revisions, what genuine evidence demonstrates each assessment criterion?
Actual final draft, earlier feedback notes.
No automatic IA mark, no copying feedback paragraphs.
Have you applied the feedback, rechecked maths, proofread and print-previewed the final file?
Done / Not yet / N/A and target issue.
No assumption feedback imported = change completed.
Have you confirmed current final deadline, identity and bibliography/format requirements?
Actual school policies if provided, existing milestone notes.
Suggested 12–20 pages and double-spacing aren't an automatic IB pass/fail rule.

Source-specific checklists are in three dedicated tabs: Maths & Technology, Bivariate Decisions, and Draft & Final Review. No prompt above should appear as a compulsory screen if irrelevant to the stage.
I'M STUCK  |  Small optional micro-prompts; choose a useful task even when data aren't available
What's making progress difficult right now?
Choose data unavailable / limited / alternate source / maths / writing / permissions / Other / Not sure
Current stage, data status, existing teacher flags
Help stays optional, short and returnable; no mark implication.
Data not available? You can WRITE your introduction in your IA NOW, using [aim], [motivation] and [beneficiary], without inventing a result.
Current aim, motivation, beneficiary, existing intro
Don't mark planned method as performed.
Can you record what you expect and WHY, or explain that you're unsure?
Use / Edit / Not sure; optional link C02
Prediction must remain tentative, not a finding.
If your expectation were true, what could that mean for the person you hope to advise?
No made-up impact or prediction forced if irrelevant.
What quantities, units, populations or specialist terms can you define before data arrive?
One useful note / Already done / Skip
No mandatory glossary or invented measurements.
Could you compare two feasible data methods or plan the first purposeful representation while you wait?
C20 method choices, C31 first-move plan
Planned methodology and diagrams aren't completed collection or observations.
This is SOURCE SEARCH, so keep candidates in private Pathfinder notes. Only when a verified source is ACTUALLY used should you write its selection rationale in the IA.
Record candidate / Check fit / Already checked
Aim, variables, relevant population, current data mode
A candidate URL isn't an IA data source until confirmed.
Do source definitions, units, population/time, accuracy, provenance and permissions support your intended maths and audience?
Short contextual source-fit checks, not one giant form
Original data design, intended beneficiary and possible sources
Don't treat a source as used until accessible and verified; cite origin.
If this source answers a DIFFERENT question, would you like to revise the aim or keep looking?
Keep searching / Propose edit / Teacher check / Save
Original aim, predictions and proposed new source
No silent plan rewrite, retain original prediction and concerns.
